conventions.convention: Joint codes are deterministic, have no feedback, use nonempty finite alphabets and positive blocklengths, and have n_k/k tending to a fixed ρ in (0,∞).
Source entropy, mutual information and channel capacity are in nats; the finite information rate-distortion function R(D) is in bits, and r(D)=(ln 2)R(D).

Lossy distortion is normalized additive distortion with a finite bound. Expected-distortion limsup and excess probabilities at every positive slack are separate criteria; exact-threshold excess convergence is not asserted.
Lossless achievability uses a strict entropy-capacity inequality, with a separate zero-entropy construction; no positive-entropy equality-boundary achievability is asserted.
Lossy budgets satisfy D≥D_min. Zero rate admits constant reproduction on every channel; positive-rate achievability uses a strict rate-capacity inequality.

load_bearing.statement: A deterministic (k,n) joint source-channel code consists of maps f_k:S^k→X^n and g_k:Y^n→Ŝ^k, with IID source law and the DMC product transition law; a code sequence has k→∞ and n_k/k→ρ∈(0,∞).

For a finite IID source and finite DMC with n_k/k→ρ∈(0,∞), zero source entropy admits zero error; H(P_S)<ρC(W) admits vanishing block error; every vanishing-block-error sequence satisfies H(P_S)≤ρC(W). The positive-entropy equality boundary is not asserted.
For every R>H(P_S), a finite IID source admits deterministic fixed-length source codes with block error tending to zero and limsup k⁻¹ ln M_k<R.

For any joint law of a finite IID source block S^k and finite reproduction block Ŝ^k, with finite nonnegative distortion and D_k=E d_k(S^k,Ŝ^k), (ln 2)R(D_k)≤k⁻¹I(S^k;Ŝ^k), with R in bits and mutual information in nats.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite entropy in nats, zero-mass conventions, directional KL and the binary entropy computations in both examples.
The external rate-distortion attainment and continuity arguments use compactness of finite-dimensional closed bounded channel sets.
The external finite rate-distortion attainment lemma applies its minimum-attainment conclusion to a continuous objective on a nonempty compact feasible set.
The external finite-alphabet rate-distortion coding theorem uses convergence of bounded IID distortion and information-density averages.

alerts.finding: In lem-it-rate-distortion-convexity-and-monotonicity, proof step 2.3 states: “I(W_k)→I(W_∞)≥R(D). Since the same subsequence of values converges to L, we obtain L≥R(D)”. However, F4 explicitly identifies mutual information as the joint-KL sum in nats, whereas F1 and def-it-information-rate-distortion-function define R(D) in bits. Thus I(W_k)=(ln 2)R(D_k), and the displayed information subsequence converges to (ln 2)L rather than L under the stated convention. The proof needs an explicit bit convention or conversion in this step; the continuity conclusion itself remains valid.

Capacities and rates remain in nats; achievable channel codes exist at all sufficiently large blocklengths, permitting the prescribed n_k. Maximal error correctly controls nonuniform source-code indices, and restriction preserves retained decoding events.

Checked the finite distortion, information and operational definitions, attainment, right-continuity and memoryless coding theorem against the consumers. The consumer preserves finite alphabets, feasible budgets, bounded distortion, bit-to-nat conversion and both separate positive-slack/expected criteria. Its converse uses right-continuity including D_min. The supplier proof's unit mismatch is separately routed as an alert.
